1. **Formation of A:**  
   Methyl 2-oxocyclohexane-1-carboxylate is a cyclic β-keto ester. Ethoxide removes the doubly activated proton at **C1**, between the ketone and ester groups. The resulting enolate undergoes Michael addition to the terminal carbon of  
   \[
   \mathrm{ArS(O)CH{=}CH_2}.
   \]
   Protonation therefore places a \(\mathrm{-CH_2CH_2S(O)Ar}\) group at **C1**, not C3. Thus A is:
   \[
   \text{methyl 1-(2-((2,4-dimethylphenyl)sulfinyl)ethyl)-2-oxocyclohexane-1-carboxylate}.
   \]

2. **Formation of B:**  
   NaH deprotonates the sole α-hydrogen of ethyl 2-ethylbutanoate, giving an ester enolate. In methyl 2-cyclopentylidene-2-phenylacetate, the exocyclic cyclopentane carbon is the **β-carbon** of the Michael acceptor:
   \[
   \mathrm{MeO_2C-C(Ph){=}C(cyclopentane)}.
   \]
   The enolate bonds to that β-carbon, and protonation gives the product in which the cyclopentane carbon lies between the two original α-carbons. This connectivity corresponds to:
   \[
   \text{ethyl 2-ethyl-2-(1-(2-methoxy-2-oxo-1-phenylethyl)cyclopentyl)butanoate}.
   \]
   The succinate-named alternative incorrectly has the nucleophile bonded to the α-carbon of the Michael acceptor.

Answer: D
